# Subsystem: pipeline (element-wise pipeline engine, op plumbing, SIMD scalar layer)

## Purpose

Fuses a tree of element-wise ops into one strided n-d loop. Every element-wise op storage
(`Op1`, `Op2`, `Map*`, `Where`, `Clamp`, `Cast`, ...) implements `read_data` as
`self.read_as_elementwise_pipeline::<Out>(index, ctx)?.to_buf(index, ctx, out)`. Building the
pipeline recursively reads every *leaf* region up front (default leaf = `read_data(.., None)` wrapped
in `OperandTyped`, `storage/core_trait.rs:123-135`; `Scalar` = `Constant` node with no operand,
`storage/scalar.rs:137-176`). `to_buf` (`storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:65-121`) allocates or adopts
the output, walks all operands (output = operand 0) with `NdIterUnordered`, optionally stages
operands into scratch, and calls `inner_loop` which pulls `[T; LANES]` through `read_bulk` and
writes it. `scalar/simd.rs` + `scalar/traits_util.rs` generate the per-type scalar fn and SIMD
`*_bulk` fn that kernels use inside `read_bulk`.

## Contracts

All `elementwise_pipeline.rs` refs below are `storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs`.

Node contract (`ElementwisePipelineImpl<T>`, elementwise_pipeline.rs:29-63, pub(crate); the pub
`ElementwisePipeline` has it as a private bound so external crates cannot implement it):
- `N_OPERANDS` (:31): exact number of `&Operand` yielded by `operands()`, or `None`. Static path:
  `to_buf` picks `to_buf_impl::<1 + n>` for 1+n <= 16 (:83-116), else `to_buf_impl_dyn`.
  `to_buf_impl` fills `[&Operand; N]` with `operand_iter.next().unwrap()` (:137) - if `N_OPERANDS`
  overcounts (`operands()` yields fewer) the unwrap panics; if it undercounts (`operands()` yields
  more) that is only `debug_assert!`ed (:138): the extra operands never get a cursor, keep
  `current_ptr == null` (:770) and a release build reads `null + offset`. Combinators:
  `n_operands_sum` / `n_operands_mul` (:943-974); `Constant` = Some(0); Vec/slice sequences = None.
- `MAX_ITEMSIZE` (:35): max size of leaves, every intermediate value and the output. Only sizes the
  contiguous lane count `8 (4 on x86) * prev_power_of_two(S::u8s::LEN / MAX_ITEMSIZE)` (:686-697,
  asserted power of two and <= 512 at compile time). Too small -> huge `[T; 512]` stack arrays per
  node (stack overflow risk), not memory unsafety. 0 -> const-eval divide by zero (compile error).
- `operands()`: every leaf that `read_bulk` touches must be yielded (cursor is only set on yielded
  operands). Order only affects dim sorting / staging heuristics; output is always index 0.
- `read_bulk::<N, CONTIGUOUS, S>(offset, status, simd)` (:58, unsafe): reads elements
  `offset..offset+N` of the current run from every child at the same `offset`; nothing is advanced
  (the Operand doc at :724-737 saying the cursor "advances" is stale). Safety (:53-57): each
  operand's `current_ptr` aligned for its dtype when `REQUIRE_ALIGNED`, and `offset..offset+N` at
  `inner_stride` in bounds of the buffer the cursor points into (original data OR a staging
  buffer). `CONTIGUOUS` promises `inner_stride == itemsize` for EVERY operand; `OperandTyped`
  (:831-858) then reads `[T; N]` at `base + offset*size_of::<T>()` and only `debug_assert`s the
  stride (:844). A stride-0 operand wrongly flagged contiguous would read out of bounds. Caller
  responsible: `inner_loop_impl` (:592-651) with `len` = chunk length, set by the drivers.
- Kernels never panic or return early on arithmetic errors: write a fallback value and OR a flag
  into `status` (:49-51). SIMD bodies and scalar fns must agree bit-for-bit and on status (tests
  `ops/op1.rs:1670`, `ops/op2.rs:1702`, `ops/op2.rs:2905`): the same element is computed by the SIMD
  body or by the scalar fn depending on its position (tail `N=1` at :638-649, `N % lanes != 0`
  fallback in `scalar/simd.rs:183,225,363`) and on strides (contiguous run uses runtime
  `SimdLevel::new()`, strided uses compile-time baseline, :664-668).
- `Op1/Op2/Map/MapMultiple/Clamp` nodes `check_dtype(T, Output)` at runtime, then
  `transmute_copy` `[K::Output; N] -> [T; N]` guarded by a const size assert (`ops/op1.rs:110-112`,
  `ops/op2.rs:166-168`, `ops/map.rs:353-355`). Soundness relies on the `unsafe trait Dtyped`
  contract (`dtype.rs:1147-1155`): equal `Dtype` => same layout, `DTYPE.itemsize == size_of`.

Driver (`to_buf_type_erased` :192-311, `_dyn` :315-444 - must stay identical):
- Region shape from `index` with `(end - start) as usize` (:200, :326, :869). A dim where every
  operand INCLUDING the output has stride 0 is collapsed to length 1 (:199-207); empty -> `Ok(())`
  before anything else (:209-211). Index validity is established earlier by the leaves
  (`check_get_range` in leaf `read_data` / `Scalar`) and by `Array::to_ndarray_buf` (`array.rs:938`).
- `NdIterUnordered::new(shape, byte strides, (itemsize, alignment) per operand)` sorts/coalesces;
  all-size-1 region reports inner stride = itemsize, contiguous, aligned (`util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:84-94`).
- Chunks of `chunk_len_max = min(inner_len, 8192)` elements (:221, `Staging::BUFFER_SIZE` :512).
  Per chunk each cursor is set to `base + offset + pos*inner_stride` (:252-275) or to its staging
  buffer with stride = itemsize; `dst` becomes a `PtrMutNoalias` (`&mut [u8]`, noalias) over the
  output chunk span (:278-284).
- `InnerLoopFlags` (:239-243): operand contiguous iff NdIter says so OR it is staged.
  `inner_loop_impl` does `assert_unchecked(OUT_CONTIGUOUS == (dst_stride == size_of::<T>()))`
  (:608): holds because the flag and `dst_stride` come from the same stride and Dtyped itemsize.
- Staging (`compute_need_staging` :467-500): (a) `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` (all targets except x86,
  x86_64, aarch64 - `util/mod.rs:641`) and operand base or any coalesced stride not a multiple of the
  dtype alignment; (b) non-contiguous INPUTS when >= 4 inputs are contiguous and they are >= half
  (:447-462); (c) inputs with inner stride 0 when `inner_len >= 64` and every other operand is
  contiguous or staged (:488-499). Output is staged only by (a); it is scattered back with
  `Staging::write_to` after each chunk (:295-306).
- `Staging::fill_from` (:530-562) caches `(src, n, stride)`; stride 0 caches with `n = usize::MAX`.
  Correct only because the first fill of any `src` is always at `pos == 0` with the full
  `chunk_len_max` (later chunks of a stride-0 operand have the same `src`). Pool buffers are
  uninitialized (`util/buf_pool.rs:37-42`).
- Status: per-chunk status ORed, `context.check_op_status` once at the very end (:310,
  `codec/mod.rs:440-447`): Error mode returns Err AFTER the whole region was written.

Output materialization (`materialize_pipeline_out_buf` :862-882, `pick_output_layout` :885-941):
- Push (`out = Some`): `out.view_mut()`, caller's strides used as-is (never collapsed unless the
  caller's own stride is 0). `check_out_buf` (`storage/buf.rs:282-297`) only checks ndim and
  writability; coverage and non-aliasing of `out` are the unsafe `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts_mut`
  caller's job (`storage/buf.rs:75-93`). Nothing checks that `out` does not overlap an input.
- Pull: dims that no input walks (all input strides 0, len > 1) get output stride 0 and extent 1;
  the rest get a packed layout in the operands' common stride order when all agree and the region
  is > 4096 bytes, else C order (:891-934). Must agree with the driver's degenerate-dim rule.
  The returned buffer may thus contain broadcast (stride-0) dims - allowed by the `read_data` pull
  contract (`storage/core_trait.rs:78-80`).
- `Operand::new_output` (:756-763) takes `base_ptr` from `data_ptr_mut().unwrap()` (panics on a
  read-only buf; `check_out_buf` prevents it) and then shares the rest of `out` for strides.

Relied on from other modules: `ArrayStorage::read_data` returns a buffer whose strides (length ==
ndim) times the requested region stay inside its data (no runtime check anywhere in the pipeline);
`NdCopier::copy` / `fill_contiguous` contracts (`util/nd_copy.rs:46-53,412-440`: in-bounds spans, no
overlap - satisfied because staging buffers are separate pool allocations);
`PtrNoalias::new`/`PtrMutNoalias::new` (`util/mod.rs:665-725`): span valid and no other access for
the lifetime; `ReadContext::allocate_buf` returns >= size bytes aligned to max(align, cache line).

Pub(crate) unsafe fns and who establishes their preconditions:
- `ElementwisePipelineImpl::read_bulk` - drivers via `inner_loop_impl`; nodes forward to children.
- `ElementwisePipelineTuple::read_bulk_as_iter` (`util/arr_sequence.rs:139-156`): same as
  read_bulk plus "drop the returned iterator before the next call" - `MapMultiplePipeline::read_bulk`
  (`ops/map.rs:338-357`) consumes it inside the call.
- `OperandTyped::new_input` (:813): "valid view of `dtype` elements, dtype == T::DTYPE". Only caller
  `core_trait.rs:134`: dtype via `check_dtype`; validity/bounds delegated to the safe `read_data`.
- `Staging::fill_from` / `write_to` (:522-588, private): driver passes in-bounds chunk pointers.
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (`storage/buf.rs:336`) and `StridedBuf::from_*` are used by shape ops,
  not by the pipeline itself.

## Unsafe inventory

- :252-256, :385-389 `base_ptr().add(offset + pos*stride)` - in bounds because offsets come from
  NdIter over the same shape/strides and the region is non-empty. Non-local: relies on each leaf's
  `read_data` buffer really covering the region.
- :261-268, :394-401 `fill_from` / :297-305, :430-438 `write_to` - chunk in bounds, staging buffer
  holds `chunk_len_max` elements of that dtype (allocated :233-235 / :362-368). Local.
- :279-284, :412-417 `PtrMutNoalias::new(out cursor, span)` - creates `&mut [u8]` over the output
  chunk while input `StridedBuf`s (often `&[u8]` slices) are alive. Sound only if `out` does not
  overlap any input: NOT established anywhere (Python `numpy(out=)` can alias a Plain input).
- :544, :550-561, :576-587 staging copies - local, but the cache at :532-536 is a non-local invariant
  (first-fill-is-full, see Contracts).
- :608 `assert_unchecked` - relies on driver flags + Dtyped itemsize == size_of::<T>().
- :620, :622-626, :630-633, :639-646 read_bulk calls and `write_maybe_aligned::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>`
  of `[T; LANES]` / `T` - alignment only `debug_assert!` (:610-612); established by staging (a).
- :837-857 `OperandTyped::read_bulk` - non-null / aligned / stride only `debug_assert`; reads `T`
  from raw bytes, so every byte pattern in the buffer must be a valid `T` (false for `bool`).
- :879 `StridedBuf::from_pool(buf, strides)` - packed permutation layout fits `nitems * itemsize`.
- `ops/op1.rs:104-112`, `ops/op2.rs:157-168`, `ops/cmp.rs:851-862`, `ops/map.rs:346-355`,
  `storage/scalar.rs:146` - transmute_copy guarded by runtime `check_dtype` + const size assert.
- `ops/into_type.rs:88,103` `assert_unchecked_eq!(inner.dtype(), ET::DTYPE)` and
  `ops/op2.rs:181` `assert_unchecked_eq!(a.shape(), b.shape())` - checked once at construction;
  rely on `dtype()`/`shape()` never changing afterwards (non-local; true for in-crate storages).
- `util/arr_sequence.rs:450-456, 574-580` Vec/slice `MapMultiple` scratch: `&mut *UnsafeCell`
  (exclusive by the read_bulk_as_iter contract), `set_len` over uninitialized `T` then indexed
  assignment (fine for Copy/no-Drop T, technically references to uninit).
- `scalar/simd.rs` and `scalar/traits_util.rs` contain no `unsafe` (fearless_simd
  `from_slice`/`store_slice` are bounds-checked).

## Edge-case surface

- Empty ranges: early `Ok(())` (:209, :335); pull allocates 0 bytes (shape-0 dims count as real).
- 0-d (`index = []`): NdIter yields one element; pull allocates one item with strides `[]`.
- Length-1 dims: dropped by NdIter; pull output keeps them real with a computed stride.
- Broadcast (stride 0): inputs - degenerate-dim collapse (:199-207) or staged fill (:488-499);
  output in push mode with stride 0 on a dim some input walks - every element written to the same
  slot (last wins), legal because the `&mut [u8]` span is computed from the stride (`util/mod.rs:109`).
  Pull output - stride-0 dims returned to the caller.
- Mixed strides / permutations / mixed itemsizes (casts): all strides are per-operand bytes with
  per-operand `(itemsize, alignment)`; dim order is lexicographic with the output first; pull layout
  follows the inputs only if they all agree (:905-919).
- Loop tails: `len % LANES` handled by `read_bulk::<1>` (:638-649); `N % vector_lanes != 0` falls
  back to the scalar fn inside `map_vectors*` (`scalar/simd.rs:183,225,363`).
- > 16 operands, `Vec`/slice sequences: `to_buf_impl_dyn` + `NdIterUnorderedDyn` (duplicated code).
- NDIM_MAX = 8: `dim_arr`/`DimArray` capacity; strides length asserted by NdIter (`nd_iter_unordered.rs:68-70`).
- Unaligned buffers: unaligned loads/stores on x86/aarch64; staging elsewhere (armv7 wheels are
  shipped, CI tests run on x86 so `REQUIRE_ALIGNED = true` paths are mostly untested).
- 32-bit (x86, armv7 wheels): `(end - start) as usize` truncates silently (:200, :326, :869);
  `shape.iter().product::<usize>() * itemsize` (:891) includes collapsed broadcast dims and can
  overflow (debug panic) even when the real data is tiny.
- Aliasing of out with inputs: no detection; see Suspicions.
- `bool` / structs with `bool`: read as Rust values from raw bytes (UB if a byte is not 0/1).
- f16 / Complex: no special casing in the driver; `Complex<f64>` (16, 8) -> 1 value per SSE vector.
- Arithmetic status: OR-accumulated per chunk; checked once at the end; nested pipelines (leaf is
  a reduction etc.) check their own status inside their `read_data`.
- Huge struct dtypes: staging buffers are `8192 * itemsize` bytes (itemsize up to u16::MAX).
- `MapMultiple` with zero arrays: `combine_hints` indexes `inputs[0]` (`storage/params.rs:845`).

## Intentional behaviors

- Rust-level binary/multi ops require identical shapes, no implicit broadcasting (`ops/op2.rs:42-53`,
  `ops/map.rs:91,165,239-247`); Python does the broadcasting. Op methods `unwrap()` and panic
  (`ops/common.rs:3-41`, `#[track_caller]`).
- Pull mode collapses dims no input walks: kernels/closures run once per distinct input element, the
  returned buffer has stride-0 dims; push mode always writes every element (tests
  `pull_collapses_broadcast_dims`, `pull_collapses_a_scalar_only_pipeline`, `push_never_collapses`
  at elementwise_pipeline.rs:1783-1882). Visit order is unspecified (`nd_iter_unordered.rs:7-31`).
- Arithmetic errors: fallback value + flag, never a panic; Ignore/Warn/Error modes decided at the
  end of the read, warnings deduplicated by message (`error.rs:273-360`, `codec/mod.rs:440-447`).
- Integer kernels wrap (`abs(MIN) == MIN`, `-MIN == MIN`, square wraps): `ops/op1.rs:327-328,
  374,430-431`; float `sign(+-0) == 0` (`ops/op1.rs:298-304`); max/min return the canonical NaN
  (`ops/cmp.rs:50-51`). SIMD fallback (fearless_simd) integer ops are wrapping as well.
- Zero-itemsize output dtypes are rejected with `UnsupportedDtype` (`ops/op1.rs:34`,
  `ops/op2.rs:41`, `ops/map.rs:237`, tests `ops/map.rs:752-792`).
- No alignment is promised for `StridedBuf` or required of `out` (`storage/buf.rs:20-22`,
  `storage/core_trait.rs:97-101`). Strides are unsigned: negative strides are unsupported (Python
  rejects them: `jix-py/src/ops/common/operand.rs:172-179`, `jix-py/src/array.rs:255-283`).
- `MaybeCompact` keeps an already-compact source untouched and ignores params (tests
  `ops/maybe_compact.rs:257-296`). `map_multiple` with one array skips the shape check (`ops/map.rs:707`).
- `Transmute` requires valid bit patterns and is an unsafe API (`ops/transmute.rs:12,53-54`).

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- Fewer lanes are used when the itemsize exceeds the SIMD width (K30). IntoType has no
  assert_unchecked any more. MapMultiple checks shape overflow with the output itemsize (K19).

### Changed in 6f8e220 (#88) and 7e93487 (#89) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- #89: elementwise_pipeline.rs and scalar/simd.rs / traits_util.rs changed for `bool8` (bool-output
  kernels, mask packing). A mask built from a raw bool8 byte must normalize it first.

### Changed in 4d11918 (#90) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `ArrayStorage` is sealed (`ArrayStorageImpl`), so the pipeline may trust read_data's buffers.

### Changed in df2f918 (#92) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `MapMultiple::new` returns InvalidShapeOperation for zero arrays (K87).
- The element cost is clamped to [0, 2^64] (`ELEMENT_COST_MAX`, params.rs), so it never becomes
  inf or NaN (K104).

## Hot spots

- N_OPERANDS / operands() agreement for every node (Op1, Op2, Where `ops/where_op.rs:371-387`,
  Clamp `ops/cmp.rs:831-846`, MapMultiple, tuple/array sequences `util/arr_sequence.rs:225,322,688`):
  is there any node whose runtime operand count can differ from its const (undercount = null read)?
- CONTIGUOUS flag: can any operand with inner stride != itemsize reach a `CONTIGUOUS = true`
  `read_bulk` (static vs dyn flags :239-243 / :372-376, single-element NdIter case, staged output)?
- Staging: is the "first fill of a src is a full chunk" invariant (:532-539) ever broken (e.g.
  stride-0 operand whose first visit is not at `pos == 0`, operands staged for both alignment and
  broadcast, chunk_len_max vs inner_len after coalescing)?
- `REQUIRE_ALIGNED = true` paths (armv7/wasm): staged output scatter (:295-306), base aligned but
  coalesced strides unaligned, `[T; LANES]` aligned stores when dtype alignment < align_of::<T>
  (packed structs), alignment of a *staged* cursor vs `[T; N]` reads.
- `pick_output_layout` (:885-941) vs driver collapse rule (:199-207): same "real dim" definition in
  every case (shape 0/1 dims, outputs of Constant-only pipelines, operands disagreeing on order)?
  Is the produced layout always a bijection inside `nitems * itemsize`?
- 32-bit truncation and `usize` products at :200, :326, :869, :875-878, :891.
- Static (:192-311) vs dyn (:315-444) duplicates and `NdIterUnordered` vs `NdIterUnorderedDyn`
  (`new_with` affects_dim_order exists only in the static one): any divergence?
- SIMD layer: `map_masks_to_bools` mask packing order (`scalar/simd.rs:95-137` narrow concatenates
  `self` then `high`), AVX2-only gating (:363), `map_vectors_different_width` chunking (:161-204);
  bool-output arms of `impl_scalar_op1!/impl_scalar_op2!` choose `map_vectors*_to_bools`, other arms
  `map_vectors*` - any kernel whose SIMD expression differs from its scalar fn (NaN, -0.0, overflow,
  saturation, status flags) gives position/stride/CPU dependent results.
- Recent churn: `4645124` (status plumbing through every read_bulk), `763a701` (Operand output
  borrows strides, NonNull staging cache), `e101fb5` (broadcast staging), `75fd25b` (runtime ndim).

### Suspicions (unverified)

- elementwise_pipeline.rs:279-284 with jix-py/src/array.rs:612-626 - `numpy(out=a)` on a lazy op whose
  Plain input views `a` (e.g. `jix.add(a.T, 0).numpy(out=a)` or shifted slices) has no overlap
  check: results differ from NumPy and `&mut [u8]` over `out` aliases a live `&[u8]` input (UB).
- elementwise_pipeline.rs:845-856 - `bool` (or struct-with-bool) leaves are read as Rust values from
  raw bytes; a numpy `uint8.view(bool)` Plain input or a crafted `.jix` file via `into_typed::<bool>()`
  makes this UB from safe code; no 0/1 validation found anywhere.
- storage/core_trait.rs:133-134 - `OperandTyped::new_input`'s "valid view" precondition is discharged
  only by the safe `read_data`; `ArrayStorage` looks implementable outside the crate (forward
  `spec()`/`info()`, `ElementTypeChange = IntoType`), so a safe impl returning a short buffer gives
  OOB reads; same trust issue for `assert_unchecked_eq!` at ops/into_type.rs:88,103 and ops/op2.rs:181.
- ops/map.rs:238-269 - `MapMultiple::new` with zero arrays panics (`storage/params.rs:845`
  `inputs[0]`) instead of returning Err; `shape()` (:369) would also index `arrays.shape(0)`.
- elementwise_pipeline.rs:891 - product includes collapsed broadcast dims: debug-build overflow panic
  for a large broadcast region read in pull mode; on 32-bit, :869 truncation can make a non-empty
  broadcast region look empty (nothing computed, 0-byte buffer returned).
